MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: (1) knowledge of pertinent laws, regulations, policies and precedents which affect the use of program and related support resources pertaining to personnel management, and a practical understanding of position management, special recruiting authorities, strategies, incentives, organizational design and position classification; (2) knowledge and skill in applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to issues concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of civilian personnel program operations carried out by administrative or professional personnel, or substantive administrative support functions; (3) knowledge of civilian personnel management policies, processes, and techniques sufficient to advise management and employees regarding rules, procedures, obligations, and entitlements; (4) ability to establish effective working relationships and to communicate with tact, creativity, and resourcefulness, both orally and in writing; including preparing and conducting formal and informal briefings, both verbally and inwritten form, with internal and external senior leadership on significant and serious matters that affect Civilian Personnel Program Management. OR EDUCATION: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or LL.M., if related. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of pertinent laws, regulations, policies and precedents which affect the use of program and related support resources pertaining to personnel management, and a practical understanding of position management, special recruiting authorities, strategies, incentives, organizational design and position classification. 2. Knowledge and skill in applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to issues concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of civilian personnel program operations carried out by administrative or professional personnel, or substantive administrative support functions. 3. Knowledge of civilian personnel management policies, processes, and techniques sufficient to advise management and employees regarding rules, procedures, obligations, and entitlements. 4.Skill in conducting detailed analyses of complex civilian personnel functions and work processes. 5. Ability to develop new or modified organizational work methods, processes, and/or procedures to improve organizational efficiency/productivity. 6. Ability to establish effective working relationships and to communicate with tact, creativity, and resourcefulness, both orally and in writing. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: THIS IS AN AIR RESERVE TECHNICIAN OFFICER POSITION. This is an Air Reserve Technician (ART) Officer position located at 442 FORCE SUPPORT SQ with the military rank of Lt Col/O-5, AFSC: 038F3. For questions concerning military eligibility please contact the Air Force Reserve Qualification Center at 1-800-257-1212. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: At least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade (GS-11) or equivalent. Specialized experience must involve planning, organizing, and managing the activities and support services of the organization. Incumbent makes technical and executive decisions on issues involved with military and civilian personnel, manpower, and services available to installation personnel, FEDERALTIME-IN-GRADE (TIG)REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-12 level. TIG: applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of a wide range of manpower concepts, principles, operations, laws, regulations, programs, and practices; knowledge of a wide range of personnel (civilian and military) concepts, principles, operations, laws, regulations, programs, and practices; knowledge of a wide range of services concepts, principles, operations, laws, regulations, programs, and practices; and practical knowledge of education, readiness, and budget execution concepts, principles, operations, and practices. MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position is: to serve as the Force Support Squadron (FSS) Commander/Operations Officer. The position is an Air Reserve Technician (ART) position. Incumbent makes technical and executive decisions for the squadron in all areas of functional responsibility Duties Plans, organizes, and oversees the full complement of activities within the Force Support Squadron. Such complements could include but are not limited to Prime Ribs, Personnel/Human Resources, Education & Training, Airman, Family Readiness, Communications, Security Forces and, in some instances, Civil Engineering, etc. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities. MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: ACQUISITION PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SPECIALIST - DIRECT HIRE AUTHORITY
MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center/AQ
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, organizing, and directing critical contractual, financial, and technical aspects of major subsystems or equipment acquisition programs through all lifecycle phases in accordance with Department of War (DoD) and Air Force acquisition laws, policies, and organizational structures. This includes experience in leading multi-functional teams of functional specialists-including engineering, contracting, manufacturing, program control, configuration management, and logistics-to evaluate contractor proposals, monitor program progress against objectives, and resolve complex, unprecedented acquisition challenges. Experience also includes preparing, presenting, and defending staff studies to executive-level government officials and industry partners, translating complex technical concepts into clear, concise communications, and establishing collaborative relationships across organizational boundaries to ensure mission alignment.. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of laws, principles, policies, and practices of systems acquisition and program management. Knowledge of business, industrial management, contracting procedures, technical concepts, and production practices to evaluate contractor proposals and activities. Knowledge of the missions, roles, functions, organizational structures, and operation of the Department of Defense, Air Force, and other entities that govern, interface with, and/or influence the systems acquisition process. Ability to communicate both orally and in writing, clearly, concisely, and with technical accuracy. Ability to establish and maintain good relationships with individuals and groups within the office, as well as, outside the immediate work unit. Ability to plan, organize, lead, and manage critical aspects of research, development, production, and support of subsystems or equipment, and integrate, analyze, and manage a variety of acquisition functions and personnel in support of the process. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Position spans the entire breadth of MAJCOM's SAP portfolio and related missions and recognized as the MAJCOM authority on cross capability and functional SAP activities. Ideal Candidate will provide senior level Program Management insight, expert guidance and advice regarding cost, schedule and performance of SAP/SAR programs to Center/MAJCOM leadership, Air Force Headquarters Staff, and/or other services/agencies. Based on unique work environment and special program requirements and processes, position requires Special Access Program/Special Access Required (SAP/SAR) experience. Knowledge of the policies, principles, concepts, guidance, procedures, techniques, and methodologies pertaining to acquisition capability development and strategic planning and programming. Specifically, knowledge of current acquisition Program Management principles such as requirements generation, funds execution, contracting methodologies, milestone approvals, risk assessments, systems engineering management, and test execution to cover the entire materiel acquisition life-cycle. Knowledge of the mission, roles, function, organizational structures, and operation of DoD and Air Force organizations to provide command level staff guidance. Ability to analyze, plan, and adjust work operations of subordinate organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within technical capabilities and available resources. Ability to communicate orally and in writing, clearly, concisely with technical accuracy to senior leaders at various security levels. In-depth knowledge of the acquisition process from developmental planning to the end of program lifecycles to support the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPB) process. This knowledge should be current and run the gamut from program office to center-level process through Air Staff and OSD process. A high degree of analytical ability to discern changes to program security levels, acquisition phases, and funding across AFMC centers and AF groups. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures to include classified areas. Ability to analyze, plan and adjust work operations of one of more organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources. Communication skills and abilities, verbal and nonverbal, in conjunction with the ability to present and influence decisions by the high levels of management, both within and outside of the directorate, and to support and defend recommendations to those levels. Skill to negotiate and/or defend findings and program support concepts and skill in preparing and presenting highly complex technical material or highly complex issues, or both, to non-specialists. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, organizing, and directing the operations of a Manpower Office, which includes exercising supervisory personnel management responsibilities to assign work, set organizational priorities, and evaluate performance. Expertise extends to applying advanced qualitative and quantitative methods, management engineering principles, and analytical techniques to conduct comprehensive studies on manpower requirements, organizational structure, workload, and program cost. Experience in advising commanders, directors, and senior staff on complex manpower and organization matters, including organizational realignment, mission changes, and resource assessment. Background includes communicating effectively both orally and in writing to deliver briefings, coordinate actions with high-level stakeholders, and resolve critical issues affecting program efficiency and organizational performance. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of manpower and organization principles, methods, processes, and analytical techniques used to assess manpower requirements, organizational structure, workload, and resources use. Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative methods used to apply management engineering principles, management analysis concepts, work measurement, program cost analysis, and resource assessment. Knowledge of the missions, functions, programs, and organizational relationships of serviced activities sufficient to conduct studies, assess manning and skill-level needs, and recommend supportable manpower and organization actions. Knowledge of manpower resource principles and techniques as they relate to organizational realignment, mission change, closure actions, outsourcing, privatization, insourcing, and related manpower studies when applicable. Knowledge of safety and security requirements, practices, and procedures applicable to the work environment. Skill in applying analytical and evaluative techniques to identify, assess, and resolve issues affecting program efficiency, effectiveness, cost, workload, manpower requirements, and organizational performance. Skill in planning, organizing, and directing comprehensive manpower and organization analyses involving diverse organizations, functions, missions, and work processes. Skill in advising commanders, directors, supervisors, and staff on manpower and organization matters and developing recommendations that are clear, supportable, and mission-focused. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the work of a small to medium-sized organization, including assigning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, developing employees, and improving work processes. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, to prepare reports, present briefings, explain complex manpower issues, and coordinate actions with customers and stakeholders. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Clerical and Administrative Support. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, coordinating, and executing military protocol activities and distinguished visits for senior executive leadership ("Top Five"), including changes of command, promotions, retirements, and executive-level conferences. This includes researching visitor backgrounds and applying comprehensive knowledge of DAF, AFMC, and civilian protocol courtesies, ranks, and precedence to prevent breaches of custom. Experience also includes managing event budgets to project and document expenditures, developing integrated execution plans under tight deadlines, and communicating persuasively both verbally and in writing to diverse internal and external stakeholders to achieve mission goals. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Comprehensive knowledge of WPAFB and its tenant organizational structure, functions, policies, and operations, etc., to ensure programs planned for visitors to WPAFB are accurate, comprehensive, informative, and are conducted within acceptable parameters in accordance with 88th ABW and AFMC policies. Comprehensive knowledge of organizational components, including the function/location/organizational structure and activities of other AFMC units, major commands, DAF, tri-service's executive and legislative liaison offices to determine types of programs appropriate for presentation to visitors from those organizations and the level of protocol courtesies to be accorded them based on rank, precedence, and significance to the mission. Comprehensive knowledge of proper civilian and military protocol courtesies to be accorded to visitors from both the United States and foreign governments that contributes to the ability to research special protocols and visiting requirements of foreign and U.S. dignitaries (etiquette manuals and guides, DAF/AFMC policies, regulations and procedures). Working knowledge of pertinent budgeting and accounting practices to project, monitor and document collections and expenditures. Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing, to achieve stated positions, or to make an adequate case for a particular strategy which may or may not be readily accepted but is the best solution to achieve overall mission goals. Ability to develop, analyze, evaluate and integrate plans and other documents related to assigned functions. Able to plan individual workload to meet deadlines. IDEAL CANDIDATE: We are seeking a candidate with a strong Protocol background: either 12+ months at the MAJCOM level or 24+ months at the Wing/NAF level. Furthermore, successful completion of the USAF Protocol Fundamentals Course and other recognized Protocol professional development curricula is highly desirable. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: US Citizen This job announcement may close at any time - apply now!
MajorDuties: Assist with implementing policies and procedures for Protocol. Plans, formulates, manages, advises, coordinates, directs, administers and executes protocol activities including: changes of command, conferences, executive level meetings, retirements, promotions, commander's call, visits by distinguished official guests and groups, special presentations and awards programs, special ceremonies, special purpose conferences and projects in support of the AFMC Commander, Command Chief, Deputy Commander, Executive Director and Director of Staff ("Top Five"). Upon notification of impending visits, plans and establishes the programming for the visit to assure senior leaders' status and prestige are maintained and enhanced. Conducts research of visitor or visitor's history, preferences and background to preclude any breach of protocol or customs and courtesies. Attends functions and monitors activities in support of the Protocol Office; briefs Commander, Command Chief, Deputy Commander, Executive Director and Staff Directorates on special functions/events, providing written materials as required on items to be requested and approved. Plans, manages, and schedules special ceremonies such as retirements, decorations, and special acts awards presided over by the Top Five. Verbally and in writing (email), accurately communicates information to command staff, internal/external OPRs, supervisor, co-workers and internal/external customers. Working knowledge of pertinent budgeting and accounting practices to project, monitor and document expenditures.

Details.JobSummary: About the position: This position is Non-appropriated Fund (NAF) and will be assigned to the Club Operations at Wright-Patt AFB. The primary purpose of this position is to provide support and assist the Club Manager in the economic and efficient operation of outlying food service operations. The position includes paid holidays, annual and sick leave accrual, as well as optional participation in Group Health, Dental and Life Insurance plans, Retirement, 401K and Flexible Benefits plans.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Thank you for considering employment with Air Force Services Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF). This position provides an opportunity to join the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base community and enjoy the many perks of being part of the team! Take advantage of activities offered through Outdoor Recreation, spend some time at the Bowling Alley, hit up a Golf Course or one of the Gyms, do some shopping at the Base Exchange, then grab a bite to eat from one of the Base Restaurants or seasonal food trucks. For those looking for personal development opportunities, courses covering a multitude of topics are available year-round. In addition, the NAF Tuition Assistance Program is available to current NAF employees with at least one year of federal service. As part of the Wright-Patterson community, we want our NAF employees to experience all there is to offer!
MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position is to provide support and assist the Club Manager in the economic and efficient operation of outlying food service operations. Monitors operations of all outlying food service operations under the club portfolio, assists at the direction of the Club Manager when and where needed. Responsible for ensuring prompt completion of monthly inventories and food track accuracy assisting with each area. Prepares reports and communicates with leadership regarding significant occurrences during the shift. Reviews the schedule of functions that are to take place during the assigned shift and ensures they are carried out as planned. Assures patron satisfaction by resolving ICE complaints and other customer problems. Provides instruction and guidance to all club staff members, including but not limited to training on proper use and adherence to cost cards and recipes; helps train and roll out new menus at each location. Makes themselves available to and provides coverage for managers and supervisors during leave or call offs to provide seamless business continuity at all locations. Assists Club Manager with appraisals, discipline and supervisory duties. Inspects and maintains facility training and safety binder information for the Clubs Collocated areas. Acts as liaison for all Public Health interactions and works with teams to ensure compliance. Provides advice and consultation regarding equipment purchases and selection of serving items as well as menu development. Interacts with vendor contacts as secondary authorized decision maker for purchasing and specifications for locations. Assists with monthly inventories, disposal sheets and transfer documentation for assets. Performs other related duties as assigned. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-13, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service: Serving as Chief, Case Writing (CW) A/B and is responsible for supervising and directing Security Assistance/Foreign Military Sales Case development and processing, including the preparation and processing of Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOAs) and related documents for Security Cooperation (SC)/Security Assistance (SA) customers. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Security Cooperation Agency. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as Chief, Case Writing (CW) A/B, with responsibility for supervising and directing Security Assistance/Foreign Military Sales Case development and processing in support of the Department of Defense (DoD), Military Services (US Army, Navy, and Air Force) and security cooperation/security assistance (SC/SA) customers.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is part of the Defense Security Cooperation Agency. DSCA's mission is to advance U.S. national security and foreign policy interests by building the capacity of foreign security forces to respond to shared challenges. DSCA leads the broader U.S. security cooperation enterprise in its efforts to train, educate, advise, and equip foreign partners. DSCA administers security cooperation programs that support U.S. policy interests and objectives.
MajorDuties: As a Supervisory Foreign Military Sales Analyst at the GS-0301-13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Analyzing, collecting, developing, and coordinating assessment criteria, indicators and procedures for timely preparation of LOA documents and providing recommendation on process improvements. Participates in the development of new policy and procedural guidance governing the management of approved Security Cooperation Programs. Assigning work based priorities and requirement of assigned work, while evaluating the overall performance of work against quality standards. Prepares and delivers data driven presentations to various stakeholders to aide in decision making and process/procedural improvements.
Details.Education: Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This is a GG-13 position in the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS). The GG-13 duties for the "Professional" work category are at the "Full Performance" work level and are equivalent to those at the GS-13 level. The selectee's salary will be set within the grade equivalent to a GS/GG grade based on the selectee's qualifications in relation to the job. To qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements describes in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. EXPERIENCE REQUIRED: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. Examples of creditable experience include: Managing technical projects or analytical portfolios within an intelligence, aerospace, scientific, or defense engineering environment; Formulating, monitoring, and executing organizational or project budgets, tracking expenditure rates, and mitigating financial variances; and Coordinating requirements with interdisciplinary teams (scientists, engineers, intelligence analysts) and support contractors. Note: Creditable experience may include previous military experience, experience gained in the private sector, or experience gained in another government agency. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of project management principles and methodologies, including planning, execution, monitoring, and closure, with specific application to complex technical projects in an S&TI environment. Knowledge and skills in developing and managing project budgets, tracking expenditures, identifying variances, and justifying resource requests to ensure projects remain within allocated funding. 2. Knowledge of the mission, role, function, organizational structure, and operation of the DoD, Air Force, and Intelligence Community; and their communication and information infrastructures and organizations; ability to interact with these organizations professionally to convey intelligence production assessments and exchange information relevant to new and ongoing intelligence analysis efforts. 3.Knowledge of contracting principles and procedures, including the ability to effectively schedule and program new and ongoing contract efforts, provide technical input for statements of work, and evaluate contractor performance. Skill in communicating effectively, both orally and in writing, with diverse audiences, including scientists, engineers, intelligence analysts, management, external stakeholders, and squadron and center leaders. 4. Skill in developing and maintaining detailed project schedules, incorporating realistic deadlines and milestones, and proactively adjusting plans to address unforeseen challenges. 5. Ability to lead and motivate interdisciplinary teams of technical experts, fostering a collaborative environment and effectively resolving conflicts within the team. 6. Ability to analyze complex data and technical information related to ballistic missile intelligence analysis projects to identify potential risks, develop effective mitigation strategies, and solve technical problems that arise during project execution. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: Program Manager (Fleet and Family Readiness Director)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes must include information which demonstrates experience and knowledge, skills, and ability (KSAs) as they relate to this position. Applicants are encouraged to be clear and specific when describing their experience level and KSAs. A qualified candidate must possess the following: At least seven years of progressively responsible experience managing multiple Quality of Life (QoL)/Quality of Service (QoS) programs for military service members and their families. A qualified candidate possesses the following: Knowledge of principles, concepts, legislative requirements, and regulations governing military QoL/QoS programs, including MWR, FFSP, CYP, and military housing sufficient to design, evaluate, and modify complex region-wide support systems that directly impact fleet and family readiness, retention, and resilience. Knowledge of and ability to utilize principles, methods, and techniques of business administration and program management. Knowledge of NAF and APF financial management policies, regulations, and budgeting processes sufficient to allocate resources, issue binding budget guidance, and maintain strict execution accountability across a multi-million dollar regional portfolio, ensuring fiscal soundness and audit compliance under shifting fiscal environments. Knowledge of evaluative and analytical processes and methods sufficient to select and apply appropriate evaluation and measurement techniques to measure and evaluate program performance. Knowledge of CNIC and region AOR organizational structure, functions, and mission. Knowledge of QoL/QoS program requirements determination. Knowledge of DoW, DON, and CNIC policy development. Skill in the use of Microsoft Office Programs (e.g., Word, Excel, Power Point, Outlook). Skill in conducting and directing complex technical, economic, and operational feasibility studies to identify cost-saving initiatives, resolve systemic or controversial program deficiencies, and optimize resource utilization. Skill in and ability to conceptualize, develop, and implement long-range strategic plans, regional policies, and organizational standards. Skill in and ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with Navy claimants, municipal/state/federal agencies, and civilian and military leadership. Ability to direct multi-location QoL/QoS programs to support force readiness and retention. Ability to develop, apply, and adjust experimental theories and plans to problems which are not responsive to resolution by accepted methods sufficient to attain program objectives. Ability to make decisions or recommendations significantly changing, interpreting or developing important FFR services policies or programs. Ability to lead inter-service initiatives, resolve deep-seated programmatic conflicts, and secure formal agreements. Ability to perform the full range of supervisory duties.

The primary purpose of this position is to provide technical direction, guidance, oversight, and leadership for Quality of Life (QoL) and Quality of Service (QoS) programs for Navy personnel and their families within the geographic area of responsibility (AOR).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: CNIC offers innovative, exciting, and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. CNIC provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. The mission of the Fleet and Family Readiness (FFR) Programs is to maximize the physical, emotional, and social development of the fleet, fighter, and family. FFR enables a ready Navy force through its Fleet Readiness, Family Readiness, and Housing Programs. We provide direct and support services to all non-appropriated fund (NAF) employees who work for Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) throughout the FFR Program worldwide. CNRJ N9
MajorDuties: In order to qualify for this position, resumes must provide sufficient experience and/or education, knowledge, skills, and ability to perform the duties of the position. Applicant resumes are the key means for evaluating skills, knowledge, and abilities as they relate to this position therefore, applicants are encouraged to be clear and specific when describing experience. Duties include but are not limited to: Serves as the principal advisor and technical expert to the Regional Commander (REGCOM) and higher Navy authority on significant and critical programmatic and policy matters related to Personnel Support and FFR operations for Navy personnel and their families. Serves as the official FFR spokesperson for the Navy within the regional AOR. Collaborates closely with regional Public Affairs Office to direct public relations initiatives, addressing complex QoL/QoS issues to cultivate community and civilian understanding of Navy objectives. Establishes and maintains high-level liaison with professional, municipal, state, and federal agency representatives. Establishes and directs regional, inter-service frameworks and partnerships to streamline program deliver and ensure a unified military social service response. Chairs regional boards of management and participates in national, regional, and local conferences to ensure consistent regional representation and alignment with Navy claimants and program managers on QoL program operations. Directs the regional execution and oversight of comprehensive Navy QoL/QoS programs including Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR); Fleet and Family Support Programs (FFSP); Child and Youth Programs (CYP); and Family and Bachelor Housing. May also include Navy Wounded Warrior (NWW) and Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Support Services (e.g., human resources, information technology, marketing, facilities, etc). Formulates, interprets, and issues regional policy, standards, and procedures governing FFR programs, ensuring compliance with legislative, Department of War (DoW), Department of the Navy (DON), and CNIC requirements. Establishes short and long-range operational plans, goals, and objectives. Continuously evaluates program performance through periodic reviews of fleet/shore requirements, personnel trends, operations reports, and surveys. Directs and supports systematic program audits, inspections, and investigations to evaluate the technical soundness, safety, and regulatory compliance of operations in the AOR. Orders operational adjustments to mitigate high-level programmatic risks. Directs comprehensive technical, economic, and social analyses to resolve complex or controversial regional issues, reduce costs, and increase quality of programs and services delivered to the fleet. Designs new organizational concepts to maximize and systematically improve operational efficiency. Exercises final regional authority over NAF FFR resources, maintaining strict oversight of execution and fiscal accountability across a multi-million-dollar annual budget. Formulates and issues annual budget and execution guidance for regional QoL programs aligned with CNIC, DON, and DoW funding objectives. Retains final review, modification, and approval authority for all NAF FFR budget submissions from subordinate commands. Mitigates financial risk and corrects operational deficiencies by continually assessing the technical and economic feasibility of operations, proactively modifying budget plans to adapt to geopolitical situations, funding constraints, policy shifts, or changing command objectives. Directs work to be accomplished by a multi-tiered workforce of civilian (NAF and GS) and military personnel. Serves as the first-level supervisor and rating official for key staff which may include one Deputy Director; at least 6, but up to 12 Supervisory Program Analysts/Managers (NF 5 or GS 13-14); and one Administrative Support position (NF-3 or IHA 1-4). Exercises second-level supervision over a diverse operational workforce, which may include Foreign National (FN) employees with various classifications, and serves as the Senior Rating Official (SRO) for activity managers within the AOR. Evaluates subordinate performance, conducts annual performance reviews, and sets clear, measurable performance standards. Exercises full authority for organizational staffing decisions, including selecting candidates for vacancies, directing promotions, and approving reassignments or organizational restructures. Identifies staff training and developmental needs, ensuring personnel receive the necessary technical and professional training to maintain high-quality program delivery. Supports CNIC's Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) policy; fosters a work environment free of discrimination, harassment, and/or reprisal; ensures all subordinate staff understand and adhere to the policy; and ensures treatment of all staff is fair and equitable.

You will need to be logged into your USAJobs account to apply. If you do not have a USAJobs account, you will need to create one before beginning the application. Follow the prompts to select your resume and/or other supporting documents to be included with your application package. You will have the opportunity to upload additional documents to include in your application before it is submitted. Your uploaded documents may take several hours to clear the virus scan process. After acknowledging you have reviewed your application package, complete the Include Personal Information section as you deem appropriate and click to continue with the application process. You will be taken to the online application which you must complete in order to apply for the position. Complete the online application, verify the required documentation is included with your application package and submit the application. You must re-select your resume and/or other documents from your USAJobs account and designate the document type when submitting your application. Failure to complete this portion will result in an incomplete application package and you will not be further considered for this vacancy. It is your responsibility to ensure your application package (resume, supporting documents, and responses to the questionnaire) is complete, accurate, and submitted by the closing date. Additional information on how to complete the online application process and submit your online application may be found on the https://help.usastaffing.gov/Apply/index.php?title=Applicant To verify or check the status of your application, log into your USAJobs account. Once logged in, the Welcome screen lists your applications, your application status and the date it was last updated. For information on what each Application Status means, visit: https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/how-to/application/status
Details.WhatToExpectNext: If you provided an email address, you will receive an email message acknowledging receipt of your application. Times may vary during the hiring process, as your application status updates/changes you will be notified with a notification letter via email.
Details.RequiredDocuments: Required documents may vary based on the eligibility you are claiming (i.e., applying as a Military Spouse Preference - MSP, applying as a veteran, applying as a current federal employees, applying as a displaced employee, etc.,). The below document(s) are required and MUST be submitted with your application by the closing date of this job announcement: Resume Your resume may be submitted in any format and must support identified the general or specialized experience described in this announcement. If your resume includes a photograph or other inappropriate material or content, it will not be used to make eligibility and qualification determinations and you may not be considered for this vacancy. Other accepted documents to support a qualification and/or claimed preference/priority eligibility may include: Cover Letter DD-214/ Statement of Service Diploma/ GED Disability Letter (VA) License Other (1) Other (2) PCS Orders Professional Certification Proof of Marriage Status Resume Separation Notice (RIF) SF-50/ Notification of Personnel Action Transcript As described above, your complete application includes your resume, your responses to the online questionnaire, and supporting documents which prove your claimed eligibility. If you fail to provide these documents, you will be marked as having an incomplete application package and you will not be considered any further. NOTE: Documents submitted as part of the application package to include supplemental documents may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove another person's personal information before you submit your application. You may be asked to provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected to confirm your eligibility.
Details.OtherInformation: Individual must fully meet qualification/eligibility/background requirements for this position. U.S. Citizens and Non-U.S. Nationals who have resided in the U.S. Territory for three (3) or more consecutive years immediately preceding the start of Federal affiliation or a signed memorandum indicating the installation's decision on the 3-year residency requirement.. Male applicants born after December 31, 1959 must be registered for Selective Service. Direct deposit is required. Satisfactorily complete an employment verification (E-Verify) check. A probationary period may be required. Pre-employment requirements must be satisfactorily met prior to Entrance on Duty (EOD). Payment of Permanent Change of Station (PCS) costs is not authorized, based on a determination that a PCS move is not in the Government's interest. Multiple positions may be filled from this job opportunity announcement. And additional selections may also be made from this job opportunity announcement. Selection(s) are subject to restrictions resulting from hiring preferences and priority consideration eligible. This is a Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) position carrying out Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR) activities for the Air Force and Space Force. Applicants must be able to provide a REAL ID or present a combination of source identity documents authorized to facilitate access to the installation. Please contact the servicing HR Office with any questions. This position will be eligible for the use of the fitness center, lodging, and many other NAF activities.
